scope: Exploratory reuse of old pilot data, never a fresh confirmation set
hypothesis: Cross-token alignment of ASTC V errors increases attention-output error beyond independent sign noise with exactly the same row energies; a causal page-mean correction may remove part of it.
primary_input: story layer17 supplied software-decoded token6 and page6 fixtures
extension_if_cpu_encoder_available: All four existing captures and six stored layers, same frozen analysis; no parameter fitting
controls: fixed exact Q/K, isolate V only
exact diagonal expectation under independent token-row Rademacher signs
256 seeded random sign trials on primary fixture
256 within-page row permutations on primary fixture
page-mean FP16 correction computed from completed prefix only
identical FP16 K/tail policy when comparing to historical snapshot
decomposition: E=B+R; report ||PB||^2, ||PR||^2, 2<PB,PR>, and their checked sum. Terms are not independent shares.
negative_outcome: No consistent positive cross-token excess, or mean correction worsens output error, or corrected ASTC remains dominated by U4 at equal or lower logical byte budget. Report per document/head heterogeneity.
decision_rule: Advance correction only if each document's aggregate output SSE improves by at least 10% and pooled relative-L2 is no worse than U4 at <=4.5 V-prefix bits; otherwise retain it as diagnostic and do not implement runtime correction.
memory: One FP16 correction per page/channel costs 16/96=1/6 additional bit per V scalar. token6 becomes 13/3 bits per V-prefix scalar; page6 becomes 25/6. Include exact FP16 tail and K separately.
budget: CPU only, at most four captures x six layers x two ASTC representations; no model download, training, future queries in correction or hardware speed claim.
limitations: Bias correction and attention error decomposition are known principles. A positive result alone establishes neither novelty nor model-level improvement. Encoder residual evaluation has nonzero runtime cost.
